label: Barnet chapel rebuilt
note: John Beauchamp, who died in 1453, rebuilt the nave arcades and clerestory of the chapel of St John the Baptist; the tower is early 15th century and the chancel about 1450. The dates are architectural estimates apart from Beauchamp's death.

label: First Battle of St Albans
note: 22 May 1455, about 15 km to the north-west along the same road: the opening battle of the Wars of the Roses. Off this map.

label: Towton; Edward IV becomes king
note: After the second battle of St Albans (17 February) Edward of York was proclaimed king in London in March and won at Towton in Yorkshire on 29 March 1461. Off this map.

label: Henry VI restored by Warwick
note: The 'readeption': Warwick, now allied with the Lancastrians, restored Henry VI in October 1470 and Edward IV fled abroad. He landed in Yorkshire in March 1471 and entered London on 11 April.

label: Battle of Barnet, 14 April
note: Easter Sunday. Edward IV defeated the Earl of Warwick somewhere between half a mile and a mile north of the town, at dawn in thick mist; Warwick and his brother Montagu were killed. The exact ground has not been found.

label: Battle of Tewkesbury, 4 May
note: Three weeks later Edward defeated Margaret of Anjou's army in Gloucestershire, ending the Lancastrian challenge. Off this map.

label: Kitts End heath first named
note: A close roll entry of 1479 names Kitts (Kicks) End heath, Bentley heath and many hedged closes north of the common: the earliest detailed record of the landscape north of Hadley, eight years after the battle.

label: Bosworth; Henry VII becomes king
note: 22 August 1485, in Leicestershire. Off this map.

label: Hadley church rebuilt
note: The church of St Mary at Monken Hadley was rebuilt about 1494, the date carved on its west tower, presumably on the site of an older church.
